question: What computer science courses address computing ethics and governance?
answer:
The strongest match is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. It requires at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Other CSCI courses that address related ethics, governance, privacy, or social-impact topics include CSCI 3410 Introduction to Intelligent Agents Using Science Fiction, which includes ethics in agent-based systems and the challenge of ensuring AI agents are safe in society, and CSCI 4245 Computer Networks I, which includes Internet organization and governance topics such as IANA, autonomous systems, internet exchange points, ISPs, certificate authorities, and BGP, along with TLS security and privacy guarantees.

For graduate students, the corresponding graduate networks course is CSCI 5245 Computer Networks I, which covers the same Internet organization and governance topics as CSCI 4245 Computer Networks I but requires more advanced graduate work.

At the introductory level, CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes common cybersecurity risks, security, privacy, and societal impacts of technology. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also addresses the broader impact of computation and the Internet on society, though it is less directly focused on ethics or governance than CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics and governance?
answer:
The strongest match is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. It requires at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Other CSCI courses that address related ethics, governance, privacy, or social-impact topics include CSCI 3410 Introduction to Intelligent Agents Using Science Fiction, which includes ethics in agent-based systems and the challenge of ensuring AI agents are safe in society, and CSCI 4245 Computer Networks I, which includes Internet organization and governance topics such as IANA, autonomous systems, internet exchange points, ISPs, certificate authorities, and BGP, along with TLS security and privacy guarantees.

For graduate students, the corresponding graduate networks course is CSCI 5245 Computer Networks I, which covers the same Internet organization and governance topics as CSCI 4245 Computer Networks I but requires more advanced graduate work.

At the introductory level, CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes common cybersecurity risks, security, privacy, and societal impacts of technology. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also addresses the broader impact of computation and the Internet on society, though it is less directly focused on ethics or governance than CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics and governance?
answer:
The strongest match is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. It requires at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Other CSCI courses that address related ethics, governance, privacy, or social-impact topics include CSCI 3410 Introduction to Intelligent Agents Using Science Fiction, which includes ethics in agent-based systems and the challenge of ensuring AI agents are safe in society, and CSCI 4245 Computer Networks I, which includes Internet organization and governance topics such as IANA, autonomous systems, internet exchange points, ISPs, certificate authorities, and BGP, along with TLS security and privacy guarantees.

For graduate students, the corresponding graduate networks course is CSCI 5245 Computer Networks I, which covers the same Internet organization and governance topics as CSCI 4245 Computer Networks I but requires more advanced graduate work.

At the introductory level, CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes common cybersecurity risks, security, privacy, and societal impacts of technology. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also addresses the broader impact of computation and the Internet on society, though it is less directly focused on ethics or governance than CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics?
answer:
The most direct Computer Science course on computing ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Two other CSCI courses address related social-impact topics. CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology, along with topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, and the Web. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles introduces the impact of computation on everyday life and the global impact of computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics?
answer:
The most direct Computer Science course on computing ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Two other CSCI courses address related social-impact topics. CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology, along with topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, and the Web. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles introduces the impact of computation on everyday life and the global impact of computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics?
answer:
The most direct Computer Science course on computing ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Two other CSCI courses address related social-impact topics. CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology, along with topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, and the Web. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles introduces the impact of computation on everyday life and the global impact of computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics?
answer:
The most direct Computer Science course on computing ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Two other CSCI courses address related social-impact topics. CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology, along with topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, and the Web. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles introduces the impact of computation on everyday life and the global impact of computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics?
answer:
The most direct Computer Science course on computing ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Two other CSCI courses address related social-impact topics. CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology, along with topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, and the Web. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles introduces the impact of computation on everyday life and the global impact of computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics?
answer:
The most direct Computer Science course on computing ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Two other CSCI courses address related social-impact topics. CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology, along with topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, and the Web. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles introduces the impact of computation on everyday life and the global impact of computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics?
answer:
The most direct Computer Science course on computing ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Two other CSCI courses address related social-impact topics. CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology, along with topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, and the Web. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles introduces the impact of computation on everyday life and the global impact of computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics?
answer:
The most direct Computer Science course on computing ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Two other CSCI courses address related social-impact topics. CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology, along with topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, and the Web. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles introduces the impact of computation on everyday life and the global impact of computing.

question: What computer science courses address computing ethics?
answer:
The most direct Computer Science course on computing ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

Two other CSCI courses address related social-impact topics. CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology, along with topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, and the Web. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles introduces the impact of computation on everyday life and the global impact of computing.

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:
The main Computer Science course that directly addresses ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

A related lower-level course is CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice, which includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology and introduces topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, the Web, and information systems. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also discusses the impact of computation and the global impact of computing, though it is not specifically an ethics course.

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:
The main Computer Science course that directly addresses ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

A related lower-level course is CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice, which includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology and introduces topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, the Web, and information systems. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also discusses the impact of computation and the global impact of computing, though it is not specifically an ethics course.

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:
The main Computer Science course that directly addresses ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

A related lower-level course is CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice, which includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology and introduces topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, the Web, and information systems. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also discusses the impact of computation and the global impact of computing, though it is not specifically an ethics course.

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:
The main Computer Science course that directly addresses ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

A related lower-level course is CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice, which includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology and introduces topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, the Web, and information systems. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also discusses the impact of computation and the global impact of computing, though it is not specifically an ethics course.

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:
The main Computer Science course that directly addresses ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

A related lower-level course is CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice, which includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology and introduces topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, the Web, and information systems. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also discusses the impact of computation and the global impact of computing, though it is not specifically an ethics course.

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:
The main Computer Science course that directly addresses ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

A related lower-level course is CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice, which includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology and introduces topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, the Web, and information systems. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also discusses the impact of computation and the global impact of computing, though it is not specifically an ethics course.

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:
The main Computer Science course that directly addresses ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

A related lower-level course is CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice, which includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology and introduces topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, the Web, and information systems. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also discusses the impact of computation and the global impact of computing, though it is not specifically an ethics course.

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:
The main Computer Science course that directly addresses ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

A related lower-level course is CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice, which includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology and introduces topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, the Web, and information systems. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also discusses the impact of computation and the global impact of computing, though it is not specifically an ethics course.

question: What computer science courses address ethics?
answer:
The main Computer Science course that directly addresses ethics is CSCI 4110 Computing Ethics and Social Implications of Computing. It is a 1-credit course covering the history of computing, intellectual property, privacy, ethical frameworks, professional ethical responsibilities, and risks of computer-based systems. Its prerequisite is at least a C- in CSCI 3710 Software Development.

A related lower-level course is CSCI 1115G Modern Computing in Practice, which includes reasoning about the societal impacts of technology and introduces topics such as security, privacy, cloud computing, the Internet, the Web, and information systems. CSCI 1110 Computer Science Principles also discusses the impact of computation and the global impact of computing, though it is not specifically an ethics course.

Text: Introduction
The Computer Operations Group (COG) operates the department’s computing facilities. Two full time employees and several students comprise the group. A large body of software is installed and maintained by this group, and direct support is provided for research projects through identification, acquisition, installation and consulting for a wide variety of software and hardware products. The COG is responsible for the Unix system administration of approximately thousand under-graduate, graduate and faculty users. Account creation, monitoring and deletion are ongoing activities. The COG home page is located at https://intranet.cs.nmsu.edu . This server is intended for the private use of the department and is accessible only by login and password. This site contains information about the hardware, software, policies and procedures related to the operation of the hosts in the domain. System problems can be reported to COG through the on-line reporting system called Bugzilla. Bugzilla allows you to submit trouble reports and recieve notification as progress is made towards solving a problems. Bugzilla is located at https://intranet.cs.nmsu.edu/bugzilla . COG’s staff members are Ivan Stranad and Mark Leisher (who can be reached via the Staff page).

Text: Getting Acquainted with the System
Check the COG Hardware Information page for the most up-to-date information regarding the computer systems in use. You should browse through the documentation available through the COG Software Information page (for local documentation). If you have a problem that isn’t addressed in the on-line manual pages, you should try one of the proctors in the undergraduate lab (SH 118). If they can’t help, or you wish to report a software/hardware problem, you should then send a workorder via Bugzilla, as mentioned above. COG receives workorders submitted through Bugzilla immediately, and deal with workorders as quickly as we can. If for some reason you can’t use Bugzilla, send e-mail to cog@cs.nmsu.edu . From past experience, we know that the answers to most user problems are contained in the documentation mentioned above. We strongly recommend that new users read the lab manual, visit the intranet web site, as that will speed up the rate with which you use the system efficiently. Also, please be aware that knocking on our door will NOT expedite the resolution of your problem; use the workorder system and your problem will receive prompt attention.
